knowledge:
- key_parameters: Data=A gene expression matrix or data frame where rows represent samples and columns represent genes ;; Labels=A character vector of conditions or disease types corresponding to the samples (rows of Data) ;; bnNum=The number of bootstrap runs for learning the Bayesian network structure (at least 100-1000 is recommended for real applications) ;; RsquaredCut=The threshold for scale-free topology fit (typically 0.8) used to estimate the soft-thresholding power beta ;; power=The soft-thresholding power beta for WGCNA ;; toCompact=A logical parameter in decision tree and one-step functions determining whether to compact the tree ;; selectedFeatures=Eigengenes used for decision trees or BN parameter fitting (can be "All" to automatically select a minimal subset)
- alternatives: Standard PCA=The documentation notes that standard PCA is not appropriate to directly apply on gene expression data due to the curse of dimensionality, whereas Pigengene applies PCA on gene modules instead ;; WGCNA=Used internally for module identification, but Pigengene extends it by computing eigengenes and fitting Bayesian networks/decision trees
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing high-dimensional transcriptomics data (microarray or RNA-Seq) with limited sample sizes to identify robust biological signatures ;; Use when comparing or integrating datasets from different platforms (e.g., microarray and RNA-Seq) because eigengenes are robust to platform differences ;; Use when wanting to build interpretable predictive models (Bayesian networks, decision trees) using gene expression modules
- pitfalls: Using too few genes=For real applications, co-expression network analysis requires thousands of genes (e.g., top-third most variable or differentially expressed genes), not just a small sub-sampled set ;; Memory and time constraints=Analyzing real datasets can take a few hours and require 5-10 GB of memory ;; Discretization warning=learn.bn may throw a warning if variables are not continuous or if there are too few unique values ;; Parallel backend=WGCNA or BN learning might run sequentially if no parallel backend is registered

workflows.name: one_step_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the entire Pigengene pipeline in a single function call to get eigengenes and decision trees.
input: expression_matrix.csv (Gene expression profile with samples as rows and genes as columns)
sample_labels.csv (A vector or data frame of sample conditions/labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Load data and format labels ;; 2. Run the one-step Pigengene pipeline using one.step.pigengene ;; 3. Plot the resulting decision tree and eigengene heatmap.
workflows.code:
library(Pigengene)
data(aml)
data(mds)
d1 <- rbind(aml,mds)
Labels <- c(rep("AML",nrow(aml)),rep("MDS",nrow(mds)))
names(Labels) <- rownames(d1)
Disease <- as.data.frame(Labels)
h1 <- pheatmap.type(d1[,1:20],annRow=Disease,show_rownames=FALSE)
p1 <- one.step.pigengene(Data=d1,saveDir='pigengene', bnNum=0, verbose=1,
      seed=1, Labels=Labels, toCompact=FALSE, doHeat=FALSE)
plot(p1$c5treeRes$c5Trees[["34"]])
dim(p1$pigengene$eigengenes)
p1 <- pheatmap.type(p1$pigengene$eigengenes,annRow=Disease,show_rownames=FALSE)

workflows.name: step_by_step_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the Pigengene pipeline step-by-step to customize parameters, learn a Bayesian network, fit parameters, predict labels, build decision trees, and perform pathway enrichment.
input: expression_matrix.csv (Gene expression profile with samples as rows and genes as columns)
sample_labels.csv (A vector or data frame of sample conditions/labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Quality control with check.pigengene.input ;; 2. Balance sample sizes with balance ;; 3. Estimate soft-thresholding power beta with calculate.beta ;; 4. Identify gene modules using wgcna.one.step ;; 5. Compute eigengenes with compute.pigengene ;; 6. Learn Bayesian network structure with learn.bn ;; 7. Fit Bayesian network parameters with bn.fit ;; 8. Predict disease labels with predict ;; 9. Build decision trees with make.decision.tree ;; 10. Perform pathway enrichment analysis with get.enriched.pw.
workflows.code:
library(Pigengene)
data(aml)
data(mds)
d1 <- rbind(aml,mds)
Labels <- c(rep("AML",nrow(aml)),rep("MDS",nrow(mds)))
names(Labels) <- rownames(d1)
Disease <- as.data.frame(Labels)

## QC:
checked <- check.pigengene.input(Data=d1, Labels=Labels)
DataI <- checked$Data
LabelsI <- checked$Labels

## Balance:
wData <- balance(Data=DataI, Labels=LabelsI, verbose=1)$balanced

## Beta:
betaI <- calculate.beta(RsquaredCut=0.8, Data=wData, verbose=1)$power
saveDir <- "steps" ## Results will be saved in this folder.
dir.create(saveDir)

## WGCNA
wgRes <- wgcna.one.step(Data=wData, seed=1, power=betaI,
      saveDir=saveDir, verbose=1)

## Eigengenes:
pigengene <- compute.pigengene(Data=DataI, Labels=LabelsI,
	     	saveFile=file.path(saveDir, 'pigengene.RData'),
                modules=wgRes$modules, verbose=1)
class(pigengene)
print(dim(pigengene$eigengenes)) ##This is the eigengenes matrix.
print(pigengene$eigengenes[1:3,1:4])

## Learning the BN structure:
library(bnlearn)
learnt <- learn.bn(pigengene=pigengene, bnPath=file.path(saveDir, "bn"),
       	  	bnNum=10, ## In real applications, at least 100-1000.
		seed=1, verbose=1)
BN <- learnt$consensus1$BN

## Fit the parameters of the Bayesian network:
fit <- bn.fit(x=BN, data=learnt$consensus1$Data, method="bayes", iss=10)

## The conditional probability table for one of the children of the Disease node:
selectedFeatures <- children("Disease", x=BN)
print(fit[[selectedFeatures[1]]])

## Prediction:
l2 <- predict(object=fit, node="Disease", data=learnt$consensus1$Data, method="bayes-lw")
table(LabelsI, l2)

## Decision trees:
treePath <- file.path(saveDir, 'C5Trees')
dir.create(path=treePath)
treeRes <- make.decision.tree(pigengene=pigengene, Data=DataI,
	       selectedFeatures=selectedFeatures, saveDir=treePath,
       	       verbose=1, toCompact=FALSE)

## Access tree results
usedFeatures <- get.used.features(c5Tree=treeRes$c5Trees[["17"]])
moduleMembers <- setNames(paste0("ME", wgRes$modules), 
                          nm=sub("_[^_]+$", "", names(wgRes$modules)))
modMembersUsed <- moduleMembers[moduleMembers %in% usedFeatures]
moduList <- split(names(modMembersUsed), f=modMembersUsed)

library(org.Hs.eg.db)
pw1 <- get.enriched.pw(genes=moduList, idType="ENTREZID", pathwayDb="KEGG",
                      Org=NULL, OrgDb=org.Hs.eg.db, outPath=saveDir, verbose=1)
